clue.text: Like Ruth in tears amid the alien corn

definitions.text: Like Ruth in tears amid the alien corn

parts.words: Like Ruth in tears amid the alien corn
parts.note: a quotation from Keats's Ode to a Nightingale, where the biblical Ruth stands weeping for her own country in a foreign field

explanation.surface: A literary allusion to the exiled Ruth weeping in a foreign cornfield.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats wrote of 'the sad heart of Ruth, when, sick for home, She stood in tears amid the alien corn'; the clue lifts that line.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth, far from her native land, was longing for her own country.

clue.text: Plant Sophy's crazy about

parts.note: the name with its S, used as letters

explanation.surface: A girl called Sophy is mad about a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyssop is an aromatic herb of the mint family.

clue.text: Swallow a drink I needed

indicators.note: needed in the sense of lacked, so the letter is missing

parts.note: a martini is a gin and vermouth cocktail

explanation.surface: Gulp down a drink I was desperate for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb about drinking; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The martin is a small bird of the swallow family.

clue.text: Girl accommodated in a cosy billet

indicators.note: accommodated in means lodged within the following words

explanation.surface: A young woman is put up in comfortable lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybil is a female given name.

explanation.surface: Everyone arrives for a purgative.
explanation.definitionFit: Calomel, mercurous chloride, was once widely given as a purgative.

clue.text: About to concede, lacking experience

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
to concede a point is to allow it

explanation.surface: Someone untried gives way in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A callow youth is immature and green.

clue.text: Cruel putting two ducks in a rustic setting

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so two of them are a pair of Os

explanation.surface: Being cruel by placing two ducks in a country scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruel' is the definition; the surface's farmyard ducks are cricket scores of nothing, each an O.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocious means wicked and brutal.

clue.text: Where the novice can save, maybe, on petrol in America

parts.note: L is the learner plate, a novice driver

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word is only one ordering of its letters

parts.note: Americans call petrol gas

explanation.surface: A city where a newcomer might economise on fuel in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' turns SAVE into ASVE. The definition 'Where' is completed by the gambling city's spirit, where a novice can gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada city is a place, answering 'where'.

clue.text: Airborne indicator Dick's now making

parts.note: the name with its S, used as letters

explanation.surface: Dick is now building a device for the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabric cone at airfields shows wind direction, hanging up in the breeze.

clue.text: Scratch game on board

definitions.meaning: to scratch about or claw at something
the word game played with lettered tiles on a board

explanation.definitionFit: To scrabble is to scratch frantically, and the trademark word-tile game shares the name.

clue.text: Legendary hunter gets the point in prayer

parts.note: Orion is the giant hunter of Greek myth
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A mythical hunter finds the meaning of his devotions.
explanation.definitionFit: An orison is an archaic word for a spoken petition to God.

clue.text: Building to look up

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to peek is to look quickly

explanation.surface: Glancing upward at a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The keep is the central tower of a castle.

clue.text: A film Rome edited once standard in France

indicators.note: edited means the letters of these words are cut and reassembled

explanation.surface: A movie set in Rome has been re-cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriflamme was the red banner carried by early French kings into battle.

clue.text: Leading characters on the staff

parts.note: reads like the chief employees of a firm, but means the symbols printed at the start of each line of musical stave

explanation.surface: The most important people working at a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Treble and bass signs stand first on each musical stave, fixing the pitch of the notes.

clue.text: Part taking in every actor alike, it's said

indicators.note: these words take in part of the following phrase, the letters sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A role that all performers would share in the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like the definition (a role) but it signals the run concealed across 'actor alike'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoken rather than written is described this way, as in testimony given by word of mouth.

clue.text: Set the compass back to front

indicators.note: to front means the first piece is put at the front, before the second

parts.note: rear means back
range or compass is extent or scope

explanation.surface: Adjust a compass so it points backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange is to set things in a different order.

clue.text: Big in Capri perhaps, but commonplace

indicators.note: in means the first piece sits inside the jumbled letters
perhaps signals the island's name is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Something is a big deal on Capri, yet ordinary elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big' reads as a description of a celebrity on the island, but it is OS, the outsize label on clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic things are dull and everyday, lacking imagination.

clue.text: A suffusion of colour in Hel land

definitions.meaning: a reddening of the face, a blush
a port town in the Netherlands, known locally as Vlissingen

explanation.definitionFit: A blush spreads colour over the cheeks, and the Dutch port of Vlissingen has this English name.

clue.text: No more than reasonable

parts.note: only means no more than
just means fair or reasonable

explanation.surface: Something barely acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Only just means barely, by the narrowest margin.

clue.text: Rope from a land-locked end less Norfolk river

indicators.note: locked means one piece is shut inside the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end less means the final letter of the river's name is dropped

parts.note: the Yare is a river in Norfolk, flowing through Norwich

explanation.surface: Rope fetched from an inland place where a Norfolk river ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land-locked' reads as one adjective, but it is LAND with the shortened river locked inside. Norfolk is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a short cord or line, as used on ships for securing things.

clue.text: Remove a number at the start

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500
off as in 'they're off', the start of a race

explanation.surface: Taking away a number at the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: To doff is to take off, especially a hat.

clue.text: Nothing to add to a plea for help, being indifferent

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
O is the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone who answers a cry for help with nothing is uncaring.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means mediocre, middling, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Go round a wizard place with a philosopher

parts.note: to spin is to go round
Oz is the land of the Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: Tour a magical land with a thinker.

clue.text: Wild herb taking in a number of Romans

indicators.note: taking in means the herb holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb

explanation.definitionFit: Savage means fierce and untamed.

clue.text: Dealer practically out of money, apparently

definitions.text: Dealer practically out of money, apparently

parts.words: Dealer practically out of money, apparently
parts.note: the agent's title looks like a comparative of the word for penniless, as if he were more out of money

explanation.surface: A trader who seems nearly bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent who buys and sells for others, such as a stockbroker.

clue.text: Does he speak sooth?

explanation.surface: A question about whether a man tells the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: Sooth is archaic for truth; one who says sooth is a soothsayer, and the grid takes just the speaking part.
explanation.definitionFit: One who says something is a speaker of it, here a teller of truth.

clue.text: Let's be honest, the average blonde's impartial

parts.note: an average blonde is fair in two senses, middling and light-haired; the 's adds its letter
fair means just and impartial

explanation.surface: Admitting that the ordinary blonde shows no favouritism.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an appeal to justice, said when insisting everyone be treated equally.

clue.text: Has about ten seconds flat to make a hat!

parts.note: a boxer flat on the canvas for the count of ten is knocked out, KO

explanation.surface: Someone takes ten seconds exactly to produce a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall military cap with a peak and plume.

clue.text: Creature wandering again and going round the bend

indicators.note: going round means the jumbled letters enclose the next piece
wandering signals the letters of the word stray into a new order

parts.note: a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: An animal roaming once more and losing its mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns AGAIN into IGANA, and 'going round' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical lizard.

clue.text: An utterance about a predator Red Indians use

definitions.text: An utterance about a predator Red Indians use

parts.words: An utterance about a predator Red Indians use

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'To Ma: hawk!' as a child's utterance about a predator; together it is the axe used by Native Americans.

clue.text: Understand the pike is thereabouts

taken as written

clue.text: He's a brute so destructive
